examples.scenario: Canonical parcel polygon is invalid but still rasterized.
examples.reason: Invalid geometry can produce incorrect spatial results; validity must pass before mask generation.

examples.scenario: MakeValid is applied silently and repaired geometry replaces the canonical parcel.
examples.reason: Any repair is derived and needs before/after digest, area and topology evidence.

examples.scenario: LINEWORK and STRUCTURE MakeValid outputs differ but either is accepted automatically.
examples.reason: Different repair algorithms can produce different valid geometries.

examples.scenario: Coverage contains a narrow overlap with a neighbor parcel but target mask generation continues.
examples.reason: Coverage overlap can alter ownership of edge cells and must be surfaced.

examples.scenario: A small gap between shared parcel edges is automatically snapped closed.
examples.reason: Coverage cleaning mutates boundaries and is QA-only unless explicitly authorized.

examples.scenario: Simplified parcel geometry is used for terminal raster membership.
examples.reason: Simplification changes vertices even when shared boundaries are preserved.

examples.scenario: Default center-based rasterization and ALL_TOUCHED masks differ at parcel boundary.
examples.reason: Boundary cell membership depends on rasterization rule and must be explicit.

examples.scenario: ALL_TOUCHED is enabled but feature ordering changes which touching parcel owns an edge pixel.
examples.reason: Input order can affect edge burn values and must be deterministic.

examples.scenario: A polygon only touches a pixel center exactly and implementation behavior is assumed.
examples.reason: GDAL notes center-touch behavior can be unspecified; terminal acceptance needs deterministic replay.

examples.scenario: Geometry CRS is implicit during rasterization.
examples.reason: Geometry-to-pixel conversion must bind the exact CRS and raster geotransform.

examples.scenario: A cutline supplied to the warp API is interpreted as georeferenced coordinates instead of source pixel/line coordinates.
examples.reason: Warp API cutline coordinate assumptions differ from the gdalwarp utility.

examples.scenario: CUTLINE_ALL_TOUCHED differs between primary and replay runs.
examples.reason: Cutline membership semantics must match exactly across runs.

examples.scenario: gdal raster clip overlapping-pixel output is treated as equivalent to center-based rasterization.
examples.reason: Overlap clipping and center membership are different selection rules.

examples.scenario: Clip bounds are rounded to whole pixels and new edge cells silently enter the parcel sample.
examples.reason: Pixel-boundary expansion must be recorded and compared to the native membership mask.

examples.scenario: A warped cutline raster is used as native terrain evidence.
examples.reason: Warping can resample, use overviews and alter grid alignment.

examples.scenario: Target-aligned pixels are enabled and assumed to align with the original raster grid.
examples.reason: Target-aligned extents do not necessarily align with the input grid.

examples.scenario: Warp error threshold uses approximate transforms and the exact parcel boundary mask is accepted.
examples.reason: Approximate transformation can change pixel membership near edges.

examples.scenario: Native center mask and independent cutline mask disagree by one cell containing the minimum elevation.
examples.reason: Any disagreement affecting extrema must fail closed until resolved.

examples.scenario: Two masks disagree only on cells that do not change min/max, so the difference is hidden.
examples.reason: Membership disagreements must remain visible even when current extrema match.

examples.scenario: Geometry digest matches after reserialization but area/topology changed because of precision handling.
examples.reason: Byte identity alone is not enough; geometry semantics also require validation.

examples.scenario: Canonical point and parcel boundary are absent but a plausible web parcel is substituted.
examples.reason: Exact target geometry cannot be inferred or substituted without canonical evidence.

examples.scenario: Numeric height difference is published before two-method parcel membership replay passes.
examples.reason: Terminal result stays blocked until canonical geometry, native raster and reproducible membership evidence exist.
